reviewer_note: This is an independent re-derivation of the CDE holiday block from the saved bytes in raw/cde-2021-2025/ (all 53 pdftotext dumps, the operator's Market Notices listing, and the CDX files), without using the block's crate_rows as a source.
confirmed_sound: Dump integrity: re-running pdftotext -layout on all 53 PDFs reproduces every saved txt dump exactly after whitespace collapse, and all 53 PDF sha256 values match provenance.json and INDEX.md; provenance.json records 22-10 as status missing with no pdf.

Independent derivation counts: 58 venue rows = 50 closed + 6 early_close + 2 unsourced, with early closes at 2021-11-26 ssm 44100, 2023-11-24 44100, 2024-11-29 49500, 2024-12-24 45900, 2025-11-28 44100 and 2025-12-24 44100; unsourced are 2022-11-24 and 2022-11-25. A row-by-row diff on trade_date, kind, close_ssm and document is identical to the block's crate_rows.

Early-close completeness: the only non-standard close instants anywhere in the dumps are 12:15, 12:45 and 13:45 CT, and they occur only in 21-06, 23-16, 24-21, 24-23, 25-37 and 25-41, i.e. exactly the six early_close rows; no notice contains a partial close the block omitted.

Window and shape: rows are strictly increasing and unique, none falls on a Saturday/Sunday, the first row 2021-07-05 does not precede the venue's first trade date 2021-06-28, and the last row is 2026-09-07.

Listing coverage: cde_notices_index.json and cde_market_notices_raw.html carry exactly 54 Holiday-category notices for the span; 53 were retrieved and 22-10 is the sole unretrieved one, so the block's '53 of 54' claim is exact.

Grid scoping: 24x7 groups (crypto from Dec 2025, Gold/Silver from trade date 2026-06-15) and the 24x5 Equity-Index PSF groups were not allowed to create rows; in every notice where those groups are open (25-18, 25-20, 25-21, 25-29, 25-37, 25-41, 25-42, 26-01, 26-05, 26-12, 26-23, 26-27, 26-27.1, 26-29, 26-36) at least one 23x5 group is closed, so the venue row is closed on rule 1 regardless.

Quoted language: missing[2]'s sentence and missing[3]'s 'will observe a normal trading day' reproduce verbatim in txt/24-26.txt and txt/24-27.txt after collapsing whitespace; the 22-10 row (id 22-10, category Holiday, posted 12/12/2022, subject 'Market Notice - Thanksgiving Holiday Schedule 2022') reproduces in cde_market_notices_raw.html and cde_notices_index.json.

22-10 absence: no pdf/22-10.pdf or txt/22-10.txt exists; cdx_ctfassets.json holds only the unrelated 2022-10E LMX program, while cdx_fairx.json, cdx_fairx_info.json (only a 22-01 MLK page), cdx_cde_notices_page.json and cdx_cde_pages.json hold no 22-10 capture; its only href is the info.fairx.com slug in cde_notices_page_20221215.html, and a live curl to that host fails the TLS handshake (error 35).

2021 id completeness: the operator's 2021 notice ids are exactly 21-01 through 21-07, as escaped table values in cde_market_notices_raw.html and as records in cde_notices_index.json; the bare '21-08' strings in the raw HTML are 'R2021-08E' and '2021-08E', and no New Year 2022 notice exists (the first is 23-01).
Document keys: every document id cited by a crate_row resolves in the block's documents map.

answers.2021-09-06_labor_day_notice_21-04: 21-04 (FairX, Date 08/31/2021, Subject 'Labor Day Observed Monday, September 6th, 2021') reads: 'Markets will be closed from 16:00 CT Friday, September 2nd - 17:00 CT Monday, September 6th. FairX will re-open for normal trading hours on Monday, September 6th at 17:00 CT for trade date Tuesday, September 7th, 2021.' 2021-09-02 was a Thursday; the Friday before Labor Day was 2021-09-03. 21-03 uses the identical construction for Independence Day ('closed from 16:00 CT Friday, July 2nd - 17:00 CT Monday, July 5th ... re-open for normal trading hours on Monday, July 5th at 17:00 CT for trade date Tuesday, July 6th, 2021', and 2021-07-02 was indeed a Friday), and 22-08's grid shows the Friday before a holiday trading normally (close 09/02 16:00) with only the Monday marked 'Closed for holiday'. The operator's language therefore supports trade date 2021-09-06 as the closed holiday trade date: the subject names Monday September 6, and the Monday-17:00 reopening for trade date Tuesday September 7 removes Monday's session under either reading of the start instant. The block's 2021-09-06 closed row is reproducible. What remains uncertain is the start boundary: the printed 'September 2nd' conflicts with the printed weekday 'Friday' and with the 21-03/22-08 pattern that closes at the preceding Friday's 16:00; taken literally it would begin at the normal 16:00 close of trade date Thursday 2021-09-02 and trade date Friday 2021-09-03 would also be closed. I read 'September 2nd' as a typo for 'September 3rd' (the Friday), so 2021-09-03 is residual source ambiguity rather than a row I can derive; the block ships no 2021-09-03 row and does not mention the typo in missing[].
answers.2022-09-05_notice_22-08: The listing subject is 'Market Notice - Labor Day September 6th, 2022' (cde_notices_index.json and cde_market_notices_raw.html), but the notice's own grid header is 'Trade Date Friday 09/02 / Monday 09/05 / Tuesday 09/06', the 'Closed for holiday' cells sit under Monday 09/05 for all three product rows, and Tuesday 09/06 is open '09/05 17:00 CT - 09/06 16:00 CT'. Labor Day 2022 was Monday 2022-09-05, so the grid governs and the subject's 'September 6th' is wrong. The block's 2022-09-05 closed row is correct; 2022-09-06 is a normal trade date.
answers.2022-11-24_and_2022-11-25_unsourced: Unsourced is justified, not rejected. The operator's own listing (cde_market_notices_raw.html) carries id 22-10, posted 12/12/2022, category Holiday, subject 'Market Notice - Thanksgiving Holiday Schedule 2022', so a special schedule for the 2022 Thanksgiving trade dates was published at T1. But no pdf/22-10.pdf or txt/22-10.txt exists (53 files in each directory, provenance.json status 'missing'); cdx_ctfassets.json contains only the unrelated '2022-10E-LMX-Crypto-LMM-Program-PUBLIC.pdf'; cdx_fairx.json, cdx_fairx_info.json (only a 22-01 MLK page plus a root revisit), cdx_cde_notices_page.json and cdx_cde_pages.json contain no 22-10 capture; the notice's only href, preserved in the 2022-12-15 capture cde_notices_page_20221215.html, is https://info.fairx.com/coinbase-derivatives-market-notice-22-10-thanksgiving-holiday-schedule-2022, and a live curl to that host now fails the TLS handshake (curl error 35). Because neither the kind nor any close instant for 2022-11-24 / 2022-11-25 can be read from the operator's bytes, shipping 'closed' or an early-close instant would be a fabricated row; 'unsourced' is the only reproducible value. The four readable Thanksgivings (21-06, 23-16, 24-21, 25-37) all close the Thursday and early-close the Friday, but that is pattern corroboration, not the cited artifact, and it keys no row.
answers.2021-12-31_no_row: No artifact contradicts the block. None of the 53 dumps mentions 12/31/2021, December 31 2021 or a 2021/2022 New Year schedule (the only '12/31' hits are 2024-12-31 and 2025-12-31 in 24-25 and 25-42); the operator's 2021 notice ids are exactly 21-01..21-07 with no 21-08, and the Holiday-category list carries no New Year notice until 23-01 (for trade date 2023-01-02). 21-07 also shows trade date Monday 2021-12-27 trading normally, the first session of the week containing 2021-12-31. So nothing in the saved bytes contradicts 'audited normal'. Caveats: the block's missing[1] reasoning is loose (it argues about New Year's Day 2022 being a Saturday rather than about Friday 2021-12-31 itself), and the conclusion is an absence-based claim rather than a positive operator statement; the block's stated residual risk (an unpublished closure or early close being under-reported) stands.

answers.advisory_non_row_observations: These do not change any crate_row but are recorded for the record: (1) the block's documents map omits three retrieved notices - 24-26, 24-27 and 26-27 - even though missing[2] and missing[3] quote 24-26 and 24-27; 26-27 is superseded by the cited 26-27.1 and neither 24-26 nor 24-27 keys a row, so this is a provenance/record gap, not a row defect. (2) missing[2]'s stated reason that 24-26 'names the crypto tier, so it keys no row' is not the operative one: the incident's 14:30 CT crypto close is later than the published 24-23 Energy/Metal close of 12:45 CT, so the 2024-12-24 earliest close is 12:45 whether or not 24-26 is considered. (3) the 21-04 'September 2nd' typo is not recorded anywhere in the block's missing[]. (4) all 53 rows' document ids resolve, and CDE-NOTICES-PAGE-2022-12-15 is the one documents entry never cited by a row.

coverage_review: Between the venue's first trade date 2021-06-28 and 2026-09-07 the operator published a special (holiday) schedule for 58 trade dates: 2021-07-05, 2021-09-06, 2021-11-25, 2021-11-26, 2021-12-24; 2022-01-17, 2022-02-21, 2022-04-15, 2022-05-30, 2022-06-20, 2022-07-04, 2022-09-05, 2022-11-24, 2022-11-25, 2022-12-26; 2023-01-02, 2023-01-16, 2023-02-20, 2023-04-07, 2023-05-29, 2023-06-19, 2023-07-04, 2023-09-04, 2023-11-23, 2023-11-24, 2023-12-25; 2024-01-01, 2024-01-15, 2024-02-19, 2024-03-29, 2024-05-27, 2024-06-19, 2024-07-04, 2024-09-02, 2024-11-28, 2024-11-29, 2024-12-24, 2024-12-25; 2025-01-01, 2025-01-20, 2025-02-17, 2025-04-18, 2025-05-26, 2025-06-19, 2025-07-04, 2025-09-01, 2025-11-27, 2025-11-28, 2025-12-24, 2025-12-25; 2026-01-01, 2026-01-19, 2026-02-16, 2026-04-03, 2026-05-25, 2026-06-19, 2026-07-03, 2026-09-07. Of these, 56 are derived as rows (50 closed, 6 early_close) and 2 (2022-11-24, 2022-11-25) are unsourced because notice 22-10 is listed by the operator but its bytes are unreachable. Every other trade date in the span falls on the venue's Sunday-Friday 23x5 grid and carries no notice, which is the block's 'audited normal' claim. The one date that deserves to be called out is Friday 2021-12-31: it is neither covered by any notice nor positively stated normal by an operator artifact - it is normal only by absence, since the 2021 listing stops at 21-07 and no New Year 2022 notice exists - and the block itself records that residual risk. A second, weaker ambiguity is Friday 2021-09-03, which would additionally be closed only if 21-04's contradictory '16:00 CT Friday, September 2nd' is read by its date rather than its weekday; the block ships no row for it. Apart from those, no date in 2021-06-28..2026-09-07 is left without either a notice or a defensible normal status.
